A user said Paperspace's boxes were great for hosting Plex servers and was sad to see the company going away.
A user couldn't create a Paperspace account because sign-up requires a phone number. Their VOIP number, used for half a decade, is automatically blocked.

A gamer found Paperspace via r/cloudygamer and used it for PC game streaming, installing Steam to access their existing library. They played Assassin's Creed Odyssey on vacation and said it worked pretty well.

Paperspace gives free access to Graphcore IPU nodes, which in theory is far more throughput than a Colab T4. In practice the user tore their hair out porting a Stable Diffusion web UI. They needed a newer Poplar SDK than the old Python 3.8 version, but the download was behind a corporate login. "That left a bad taste in my mouth."
A user said Paperspace locked or froze their account but kept charging them. They didn't notice for a while because they rarely used it, and support ignored their questions.
In college, a user's autonomous-driving research project received a few thousand dollars in compute credits from Paperspace to help with training costs.

A user runs Stable Diffusion on Paperspace's $9/mo Pro tier, which gives up to 6 hours of GPU time without per-usage billing. That avoids electricity costs in the EU and their aging home Vega GPU. They worry the plan will be replaced by strict per-usage pricing.

A user called Gradient Notebooks a worse version of Google Colab and useless for serious DL work. They said Core servers had very slow internet, so copying datasets took forever. SSH access was an uphill battle, with a confusing virtual console and GUI instead. The docs were outdated and sometimes wrong. They switched to Lambda and Vast.ai and "never looked back."

A user runs personal ML projects on a Paperspace VM plus Parsec. By their math, the hourly rate for a standard GPU VM beats buying a local machine, without the complexity of ML workflow tools. As a bonus, they reuse the VMs for hobby gaming.

A user said Colab, Kaggle and Paperspace can be "_okay_" as dev environments when you can't afford a local GPU. They noted that having a local GPU is effectively a requirement for real development work.

A user struggled to run anything but the smallest Dolly model on Paperspace. Loading dolly-v2-6-9b via an HF pipeline crashed the kernel on a Quadro P6000 with 24GB. They called it "the most difficult experience I've ever had trying to do basic inference."
A user had so much trouble with Paperspace's notebook system that they gave up. In retrospect, they admitted it was partly their own fault for not using generator functions to control memory bloat.
